newsitem.title: FRANCE: Primakov says NATO-Russia deal possible on Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Primakov says NATO-Russia deal possible on Tuesday.

text.p: Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov said on Monday he hoped to complete a draft agreement on future partnership between NATO and Russia in talks with the alliance's secretary-general on Tuesday.

Primakov told a news conference in Strasbourg before he meets NATO chief Javier Solana in Luxembourg on Tuesday: "I want this meeting to be the last one and to enable us to sign (a NATO-Russia agreement) on May 27. The possibility of signing the document will be totally cleared up tomorrow."

The Russian minister was speaking after talks with the so-called troika of past, present and future holders of the European Union's rotating presidency, headed by Dutch Foreign Minister Hans Van Mierlo.

Primakov repeated Moscow's ritual denunciation of NATO plans to admit former Soviet bloc central European countries as "the most serious error since the end of the Cold War", but added that a Russia-NATO document should minimise the repercussions on Russian security.

President Boris Yeltsin has agreed in principle to sign an agreement with the 16-nation Atlantic Alliance in Paris on May 27 but U.S. and NATO officials have repeatedly expressed caution as to whether it would be ready in time.

The West has rejected Russian demands for legal commitments not to station nuclear or conventional forces on the territory of new NATO members or to build military infrastructure there, but it has said it has no plans to deploy nuclear weapons or permanently stationed forces there at present.
